newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dollar to spur Wolters, stg to brake Reed Elsevier.
newsitem.headline: Dollar to spur Wolters, stg to brake Reed Elsevier.

text.p: Professional publishers Wolters Kluwer and Reed Elsevier, both due to post first-half figures next week, are expected to show markedly different effects from the current strength of the dollar and sterling.
Analysts expect the firm dollar to contribute to a rise of almost 20 percent in first-half net profit for Wolters Kluwer which will report results on Tuesday.
First-half net profits from ordinary operations at are seen rising to 235-253 million guilders ($113-122 million), with a consensus at 245 million, up from 206 million a year earlier.
But the strong pound sterling is seen holding back first half earnings growth to around six percent at Anglo-Dutch Reed Elsevier which reports on Thursday.
Reed Elsevier's headline pre-tax profit is forecast at 423-460 million sterling, with a consensus at 441 million, versus 416 million in the first half of 1996.
Wolters Kluwer is expected to return to its familiar path of double-digit annual earnings per share growth at a slightly faster rate than its own official forecast of 15 percent.

Earnings growth slowed to six percent in 1996 due to accounting changes linked to the company's $1.9 billion acquisition of U.S. tax publisher CCH, but management stressed this was a temporary hiatus.

The CCH acquisition boosted the proportion of group sales and profits made in North America to around 30 percent from 10 percent, leaving Wolters Kluwer is well-placed to benefit from the recent appreciation of the dollar.

Analysts said first-half results would also reflect further improvement of margins at CCH, good organic growth at other Wolters Kluwer businesses and contributions from a string of smaller niche publishers acquired since the CCH deal.
Reed Elsevier's businesses were also performing well in local currency terms, analysts said, but the translation into sterling will counteract the bottom line effect.
In contrast, half earnings per share in guilders for Elsevier -- the group's Dutch parent company -- are expected to rise some 20 per cent.

Investment in on-line electronic delivery systems is also checking the pace of earnings growth, but analysts say this will strengthen Reed Elsevier in the long term. Recent acquisitions in scientific, legal and business publishing are expected to boost earnings from the second half of 1997.

After consistently outperforming the Dutch market over the past 10 years, Wolters Kluwer and Elsevier lagged a 33 percent rise in the AEX index in the first half of 1997 with relatively modest rises of four and 12 percent respectively.

In July the shares performed more in line with the 14 percent rise of the index, possibly aided by Outperformer ratings for both stocks (as well as for the Reed share, listed in London) issued by analysts at Goldman Sachs.
Andre Moons at ING Barings said he expected Wolters Kluwer and Elsevier to re-establish their credentials as market outperformers and rates them both a Buy.
"After the severe underperformance so far this year their current valuations are certainly not overstretched," he said. ($ = 2.079 Dutch Guilders)
